title: Responsible AI & the Rules
summary: Bias, transparency, human oversight, and the frameworks and laws shaping AI.

lessons.title: What 'responsible AI' means
points: NIST's AI Risk Management Framework describes trustworthy AI as: valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed.
Responsible AI means designing, using and monitoring AI so these qualities hold up in the real world.

lessons.title: Bias and fairness
points: AI learns from data, and data can reflect historical unfairness, which models may repeat or amplify.
High-impact uses such as hiring, lending, healthcare and policing need testing for unfair outcomes across groups.
Keep a human in the loop for decisions that significantly affect people.

lessons.title: Frameworks: NIST AI RMF & ISO/IEC 42001
points: The NIST AI RMF 1.0 (January 2023) is voluntary and organised around four functions: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.
NIST AI 600-1 (July 2024) is a Generative AI Profile that applies the framework to generative AI risks.
ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is an international standard for an AI management system, similar in style to ISO/IEC 27001 for security.

lessons.title: Law: the EU AI Act
points: The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and uses a risk-based approach: unacceptable, high, limited (transparency) and minimal risk.
Bans on certain prohibited practices, and an AI literacy duty for providers and deployers, have applied since 2 February 2025.
Rules for general-purpose AI model providers have applied since 2 August 2025, and most other rules since 2 August 2026. A 2026 amendment moved many high-risk rules to December 2027 and August 2028.
lessons.tip: Even outside the EU, these ideas (transparency, human oversight, risk assessment) are becoming normal expectations.

questions.q: What are the four core functions of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
questions.why: The AI RMF 1.0 core is organised into Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.

questions.q: The NIST AI RMF is a mandatory law for all organisations worldwide.
questions.why: The AI RMF is voluntary guidance. Laws like the EU AI Act are a separate matter.

questions.q: How can bias enter an AI system?
options: Through training data that reflects historical or sampling bias, and through design choices
It cannot: AI is always neutral
Only through the user's screen settings
questions.why: Biased or unrepresentative data and design decisions can lead to unfair outcomes.

questions.q: What approach does the EU AI Act take?
options: A risk-based approach with stricter rules for higher-risk uses
It has no rules, only advice
questions.why: The Act sorts AI uses by risk, from prohibited practices to minimal-risk uses with few obligations.

questions.q: The EU AI Act's prohibitions and AI literacy obligations have applied since 2 February 2025.
questions.why: Those first provisions became applicable on 2 February 2025, six months after entry into force on 1 August 2024.

questions.q: An AI tool screens job applicants. What is the most responsible practice?
options: Let it reject candidates automatically with no review
Test for unfair outcomes and keep meaningful human review of decisions
Train it only on past hires without checking
questions.why: Hiring is high-impact. Bias testing, transparency and human oversight are key safeguards.

options: An international standard for AI management systems
questions.why: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 specifies requirements for establishing and improving an AI management system.

questions.q: Telling people when they are interacting with an AI system is a common transparency expectation.
questions.why: Transparency, including disclosure of AI interaction and AI-generated content, appears in frameworks and in the EU AI Act.

questions.q: Which of these is listed by NIST as a characteristic of trustworthy AI?
questions.why: NIST's trustworthy characteristics include accountable and transparent, along with valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, explainable, privacy-enhanced, and fair.

questions.q: What does 'human in the loop' mean?
options: A person reviews or approves the AI's important outputs or actions
The AI runs on a person's laptop
questions.why: Human oversight lets people catch errors and harms before they have impact.
